property_summary: For any initial owner and any new owner, calling setOwner(newOwner) must change owner to newOwner; the mutant returns true but leaves owner unchanged.
After a successful setOwner call by the current owner, the owner must equal the new owner passed to the call; the mutant returns success but does not update owner.
After a successful setOwner call, the new owner must equal the _owner argument passed; the mutant always sets it to msg.sender, violating this rule.
The owner after a successful setOwner call must equal the provided _owner parameter; the mutant always sets owner to address(0) breaking this invariant.

Only the current owner can change the owner; without the onlyOwner check, a non-owner can call setOwner and change owner, violating that exactly one assertion after any call returns the expected boolean based on caller identity.
After any call to setOwner, the new owner must equal the msg.sender of that call. The bug removes the onlyOwner check, allowing a caller to successfully set an owner different from themselves.
For any caller, a call to setOwner(x) must succeed if and only if msg.sender is the current owner; the bug removes this check, allowing a non-owner to succeed and change owner to x.

For any caller that is not the original owner, setOwner(x) must always revert; the correct contract enforces this via the onlyOwner modifier, while the buggy version makes it revert for all callers, preventing even the real owner from updating the owner.
The owner can always update the owner to a new address, but the bug causes every setOwner call to revert, so the owner cannot be updated.
For any caller that is the current owner, a successful setOwner call must return true; the mutant returns false instead.
When called by the owner, setOwner must return true after updating the owner.

After any call to setOwner by any address, the owner in the reference contract remains unchanged unless the caller is the current owner, while in the mutant any caller can change the owner, so a non-owner caller can successfully update owner.

After any call to setOwner by a non-owner, the owner address must remain unchanged; the buggy version incorrectly updates owner to msg.sender even when msg.sender is not the original owner, causing an ownership change when it should revert.
After a successful call to setOwner by the current owner, the owner must become the _owner argument; the buggy version incorrectly sets owner to msg.sender instead.
A non-owner caller can successfully change the owner via setOwner, breaking the invariant that only the current owner can update the owner address.
After any call to setOwner, the owner must equal the msg.sender; the buggy modifier allows any caller to change owner to any address, violating this rule.
In the reference contract, any call to setOwner made by a non-owner address will revert, whereas in the buggy contract, such a call will succeed and change the owner.
